column1: # Synthetic AS table fixture — issue #23 / ADR-0044.
# EVERY address here is documentation space and every AS number is documentation
# space. Nothing in this file describes real allocations, and nothing in it
# describes this project's infrastructure:
#   - 2001:db8::/32                                   documentation prefix (RFC 3849)
#   - AS64496–AS64511                                 documentation ASNs (RFC 5398)
# A real routing-table excerpt would carry real allocations into a public repo, so
# this is built by hand instead. It is shaped to exercise the cases the diversity
# control actually turns on, not to resemble a real table:
#   - AS64496 announces TWO disjoint ranges, in different /24s. That is the shape
#     the whole control exists to catch: one operator behind two directory entries
#     that share no visible label. A test that only ever puts one prefix in one AS
#     never proves the check rejects anything.
#   - Several single-range ASes, so a diverse chain is actually available and a
#     rejection can be told apart from an empty candidate set.
#   - IPv6, so the v6 family is not dead code.
#     2001:db8:ffff::/48 and everything else) so the unknown answer is reachable
#     from an address that is otherwise perfectly ordinary.
# --- AS64496: one AS, two ranges, two different /24s ---
# --- distinct single-range ASes ---
